summary: Full-extraction pass over 7 stored Seychelles documents: two FinCEN advisories on the 1995 Economic Development Act (already in the events), the Immigration Department fee list, the 2013 permanent-residence guideline and quick guide, the 2014 special-circumstances citizenship form, and the residence permit web page. Adds the investor rules not yet recorded (residence and business-association periods, exam pass mark, sponsors, absence limits, processing fees, the investor PR fee from the 2020 list). No statistics exist in any of these documents.

ledger.contains: FinCEN advisory (March 1996) telling US banks to scrutinise Seychelles transactions after the FATF condemned the 1995 Economic Development Act, which let investors of at least USD 10 million in approved investments obtain immunity from prosecution and asset forfeiture; attached OECD/FATF press release of 1 Feb 1996 (FATF then of 26 countries; list of members). The Act is not a residence or citizenship programme in our list (no programme id), so the USD 10 million threshold is recorded only in the existing event; nothing else in scope.

FinCEN Advisory 2W (May 2003) withdrawing the 1996 advisory because Seychelles repealed the 1995 Economic Development Act (USD 10 million investors; repeal date not given); the FATF had withdrawn its warning too. Already recorded as an event; nothing else in scope.

Immigration Department fee list (2020): permanent residence permit fees by category (investors SCR 150,000; marriage, priority worker, student), ordinary residence permit SCR 150,000 for 5 years plus SCR 75,000 spouse and SCR 25,000 per child, Eden Island Scheme SCR 150,000 for 5 years incl. spouse and children, dependent permit, citizenship fees incl. special circumstances investors SCR 350,000, SCR 1,000 processing fee on all applications; plus GOP, visitor permit, civil status, ID card and passport fees (out of scope). Adds the investor PR fee and the processing fee for the three programmes; the Eden Island and investor-citizenship fees were already recorded.

Form IMM-15 notes (Dec 2013): permanent residence criteria and fees for marriage, priority worker, student and investor categories; investors USD 1 million plus 1 year residence or 5 years' business association, permit fee SR 150,000 (already recorded), processing fee SR 1,000, benefits (work without GOP, 50% property sanction fee, children endorsed to 18, no free health care), documents required. Non-investor categories out of scope. All investor rules now recorded.

Department's quick guide (Nov 2013, 19 pages) to the 2013 amendments: permanent residence and citizenship criteria by category (marriage, priority worker, student, investor), general conditions (absence up to 1 year, no prison over 1 year, citizenship exam over 80%), rights of permanent residents and citizens, deprivation and renunciation, and fictional example cases (incl. an investor with USD 500,000 not eligible, and a USD 1.5 million Eden Island villa owner eligible only for a residence permit because a private residence is not a direct investment). Investor rules recorded (USD 1 million, 1 year residence or 5 years' association, 11 years for citizenship, exam, absence limit, sanction-fee benefit); the example amounts are illustrations, not rules, so not recorded. Images are photos only.

Form IMM2 notes (Feb 2014) for citizenship under special circumstances (Citizenship Act s. 5(2), 5A-5C): criteria for marriage, students, priority workers, investors (USD 1 million in a business plus 11 years' aggregate residence) and former citizens; three sponsors, newspaper and Gazette notices, 80% in the citizenship exam, no prison sentence of 1 year or more, no continuous absence of 1 year without permission, SR 1,000 processing fee. All investor-relevant rules recorded.

Immigration Department web page on the ordinary Residence Permit (captured 2026): criteria (family connection or special contribution), no right to work, proof of financial status, conditions (5 days' residence per 12 months, bank guarantee of at least SCR 20,000, no free health care or social security), processing fee SCR 1,000, permit fee SCR 150,000 for 5 years, SCR 75,000 spouse, SCR 25,000 per child. Does not mention Eden Island or any investment amount. Conditions and processing fee recorded under the Eden Island programme with a caveat; the ordinary-permit fees are not the Eden Island fees (the 2020 list prices that scheme separately) so they are not recorded.
